title: Height after removing a subtree
description_html:
You are given a rooted tree with n nodes (root = node 1), described by parent-child edges. Removing a node deletes that node together with its entire subtree (all of its descendants). Given a node v to remove, return the height (max number of edges from the root to any remaining node) of the tree that remains.

Follow-up: answer the query for every node v efficiently (i.e. for each v, the height after removing subtree(v)).

Input

n
n-1 lines: edges  u v
v            # node to remove (with its subtree)

Output

One integer: the height of the remaining tree (0 if only the root remains; the root itself cannot be removed in the single-query form).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5.

Example

5
1 2
1 3
3 4
4 5
4            # remove node 4 and its subtree {4,5}
----
1

Remaining nodes {1, 2, 3}; deepest remaining path 1 → 3 (or 1 → 2) = 1 edge.

See Notes for the single-removal and all-removals (re-rooting / Euler-range) approaches, the trio, and references.
